q1: SELECT A.PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(B.EXPERIENCE_YEARS), 2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT AS A INNER JOIN EMPLOYEE AS B ON A.EMPLOYEE_ID = B.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY A.PROJECT_ID
q2: SELECT PROJECT_ID, IFNULL(ROUND(EX / EM, 2), 0.00) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM ( SELECT P.PROJECT_ID, SUM(E.EXPERIENCE_YEARS) AS EX, COUNT(P.EMPLOYEE_ID) AS EM FROM PROJECT P JOIN EMPLOYEE E USING (EMPLOYEE_ID) GROUP BY P.PROJECT_ID ) AS T
q1_prompt_sql: SELECT A.PROJECT_ID, ROUND(AVG(B.EXPERIENCE_YEARS), 2) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM PROJECT AS A INNER JOIN EMPLOYEE AS B ON A.EMPLOYEE_ID = B.EMPLOYEE_ID GROUP BY A.PROJECT_ID
q2_prompt_sql: SELECT PROJECT_ID, IFNULL(ROUND(EX / EM, 2), 0.00) AS AVERAGE_YEARS FROM ( SELECT P.PROJECT_ID, SUM(E.EXPERIENCE_YEARS) AS EX, COUNT(P.EMPLOYEE_ID) AS EM FROM PROJECT P JOIN EMPLOYEE E USING (EMPLOYEE_ID) GROUP BY P.PROJECT_ID ) AS T
explanation: Both queries aim to calculate the average years of experience for employees assigned to each project. They join the PROJECT and EMPLOYEE tables on EMPLOYEE_ID, group the results by PROJECT_ID, and compute the average of EXPERIENCE_YEARS. The difference in syntax (Q1 uses AVG() and ROUND(), while Q2 uses SUM() and COUNT() with an IFNULL()) does not change the outcome as long as the data is consistent.
